  3. 3exit 125: skip, cannot test
  4. 4any other code: abort

A bug appeared somewhere in sixteen commits.

Git bisect finds the first bad commit by halving the range.

You start bisect and mark both ends of the range.

HEAD, commit sixteen, is bad.

Commit one is good.

Git then checks out the middle commit.

Each answer you give halves the suspect range.

Commit eight is good, twelve is bad,

ten is good, eleven is bad.

Four tests are enough.

After the last answer,

Git reports commit eleven as the first bad commit.

Then git bisect reset returns you to where you started.

A test script can give the answers with git bisect run.

Exit zero means good.

One to one hundred twenty seven means bad,

except one twenty five, which means skip.

Any other code aborts.
